newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Lanka Central Bank plays down forex fraud reports.
newsitem.headline: Lanka Central Bank plays down forex fraud reports.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Central Bank said on Friday that recent news reports of alleged foreign exchange fraud at a private commercial bank were no cause for alarm.

"The Central Bank wishes to assure the public that there should be no cause for concern or alarm, relating to the financial stability of the bank concerned or for the banking system in general, arising from the matter under investigation," the bank said in a statement.
The Central Bank did not identify the bank.
On Wednesday, the state-owned Daily News said a top official of a private bank was questioned by police over a foreign exchange fraud. The newspaper did not identify the bank.

The newspaper said on Thursday police offered a 750,000 rupee reward for information leading to the arrest of two private bank employees in connection with the embezzlement of 12.8 million rupees. The paper identified the employees but not the bank.

The Central Bank said the newspaper reports appeared to be based on an investigation by Customs and Exchange Control departments after a person was found trying to take foreign currencies out of the country without due authority.
